*Reasoning as the farmer:*

Alright, let me think about this year on my 4.1 mu. Me and the old lady are the only ones here — the kids are all in the city working, they send money at New Year but they're not coming back to farm. At 78 I'm slower than I used to be, but this land has fed us for my whole life and I know every corner of it.

I'll do what I've always done. About 3 mu is the wheat-maize rotation — that's the main thing, keeps grain in the house and a bit to sell. The other 1.1 mu is my cotton plot, the same piece of ground I've been putting cotton on for forty years. I know some of the young ones switched to all grain because cotton picking is hard work, but that plot grows cotton best and I'm not going to change now. When picking comes in September I'll pay my nephew 100 yuan a day for a few days to help us finish.

**Wheat (3 mu):** I plant around October 10-15, right after the maize comes off. I use a local improved variety — I buy new seed every two or three years, otherwise save my own. Before planting I broadcast about 50 kg of the 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu and plow it in. Then at jointing in March, if the wheat looks a bit yellow I topdress maybe 10 kg of urea per mu. So total N works out around 17-18 kg per mu. That's what the extension fellow told me years back and it gives me about 420 kg per mu most years. I irrigate three times — once before winter so the roots don't freeze, once at jointing, once at grain fill. Each irrigation costs money at the well meter, so I don't waste water. I'll spray herbicide once in spring for the grass weeds.

**Maize (3 mu, same land after wheat):** This is the tight part — wheat off around June 8, maize has to go in by June 15 or I lose yield. No time for deep tillage, I just run the rotary tiller shallow and plant. I use a local improved seed, about 3 kg per mu. I don't buy the expensive hybrid seed the business farms use — costs twice as much and for my land the difference isn't worth it. About 15 kg N per mu — half at planting as compound, half as urea at the big trumpet stage in late July. One irrigation usually, sometimes two if July is dry. Herbicide once after emergence. I expect around 450 kg per mu.

**Cotton (1.1 mu):** Plant late April when the soil warms up. I use a basic Bt cotton variety, saves me spraying so much for bollworm. Apply about 10 kg N per mu — cotton doesn't need as much as grain. I till the plot deeper than the grain fields, plow it in early April. Two irrigations: one around flowering in July, one when the bolls are filling in August. I spray for aphids and bollworm maybe three times through the summer, and a herbicide early on. Picking starts early September and goes into mid-October — this is the hardest part, my back can't do what it used to, so my nephew helps for a week. I hope for around 220 kg of lint per mu.

I'm not trying anything new this year. Prices for cotton have been mediocre, but I'll stick with it. If grain prices drop I still have cotton; if cotton fails I still have the wheat and maize. That's how I've always done it.
